title: React.js Component Architecture & Hooks Assessment
description: Test your understanding of component lifecycle, state management, useEffect dependencies, and performance optimizations.

questions.questionText: Which React hook should be used to avoid recalculating an expensive computation on every render?
questions.explanation: useMemo returns a memoized value that only recalculates when one of its specified dependencies changes.

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between controlled and uncontrolled form components in React?
options: Controlled components use Redux while uncontrolled use local state
Controlled components have their value handled by React state, while uncontrolled rely on DOM refs
Uncontrolled components are faster and cannot have default values
Controlled components only work with class components
questions.explanation: In a controlled component, form data is handled by React state. In uncontrolled components, form data is handled by the DOM itself using refs.

questions.questionText: When does the cleanup function returned inside a useEffect hook execute?
options: Only when the browser window closes
Before the component re-renders or unmounts
Only when an uncaught error occurs in the component
questions.explanation: The cleanup function runs before the component is removed from the UI (unmounts) and prior to running the effect again on re-render.

title: Node.js & Express RESTful APIs Diagnostic
description: Evaluate your knowledge of the Node.js event loop, Express routing, middleware execution order, and error handling.

questions.questionText: In an Express application, what parameter signature distinguishes error-handling middleware from regular middleware?
questions.explanation: Express recognizes error-handling middleware by its four arguments: (err, req, res, next).

questions.questionText: Which HTTP method should be used when an API endpoint performs a partial update of a resource?
questions.explanation: PATCH is standard for partial updates, whereas PUT is traditionally used for replacing the entire entity.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of process.nextTick() in Node.js?
options: It delays execution until the next calendar day
It schedules a callback to be run at the very end of the current phase of the event loop before I/O
It creates a new thread in the worker pool
questions.explanation: process.nextTick() queues a callback function to be invoked immediately after the current operation finishes and before the event loop continues.

title: Python Core & Data Analysis Fundamentals
description: Assess list comprehensions, dictionary operations, Pandas DataFrame manipulation, and exception handling.

questions.questionText: In Pandas, which method is used to remove rows containing null/NaN values from a DataFrame?
questions.explanation: df.dropna() drops rows (or columns) that contain missing or NaN values.

questions.questionText: What does the *args parameter syntax in a Python function definition permit?
options: An arbitrary number of positional arguments passed as a tuple
Array slicing in the function body
questions.explanation: *args allows passing a variable number of positional arguments to a function, accessible as a tuple.

title: Java Core & Object-Oriented Principles
description: Test OOP fundamentals (Inheritance, Polymorphism, Abstraction, Encapsulation), Collections, and Exception Handling.

questions.questionText: Which collection implementation in Java maintains elements in sorted order based on their natural comparison or a Comparator?
questions.explanation: TreeSet is part of the NavigableSet interface in Java and guarantees that elements are maintained in sorted ascending order.

questions.questionText: Can an abstract class in Java have concrete methods with complete method bodies?
options: No, abstract classes can only contain method signatures
Yes, an abstract class can contain both abstract and concrete methods
Only if the class is declared static
Only in Java versions prior to Java 7
questions.explanation: Abstract classes in Java can have fully implemented concrete methods alongside abstract methods.

title: MongoDB & Database Architecture Assessment
description: Assess schema design patterns, aggregation stages, compound indexing, and embedding versus referencing tradeoffs.

questions.questionText: In a MongoDB aggregation pipeline, which stage performs a left outer join with another collection in the same database?
questions.explanation: $lookup performs an equality match or subquery join between documents from the input and another collection.

questions.questionText: What is the primary benefit of creating a compound index on { department: 1, graduationYear: -1 } in MongoDB?
options: It encrypts documents belonging to both fields
It allows queries filtering by department, or by department AND graduationYear, to use index scans instead of collection scans
It automatically converts strings to numbers
questions.explanation: A compound index supports queries that match on the prefix (department) or both fields in the index key pattern.

title: Modern JavaScript (ES6+ & Async Architecture)
description: Test your understanding of JavaScript closures, prototypical inheritance, event loop phases, and async/await mechanics.

questions.questionText: What is the output of `typeof NaN` in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, NaN represents "Not-a-Number", but its primitive data type according to the ECMAScript spec is number.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes how closures function in JavaScript?
options: Closures prevent functions from accessing variables defined outside their body
A closure is the combination of a function bundled together with references to its surrounding lexical environment
Closures are only created when using arrow functions
Closures immediately execute and discard local memory variables
questions.explanation: A closure gives a function access to its outer scope from an inner function, preserved across invocations.

questions.questionText: Which event loop queue takes priority when synchronous code finishes execution?
questions.explanation: The microtask queue (promise callbacks) is drained completely before the next macrotask is processed.

title: C++ Systems & Memory Management Competency
description: Assess pointer arithmetic, dynamic heap allocation, references, virtual destructors, and RAII principles.

questions.questionText: Why should a base class containing virtual methods declare a virtual destructor in C++?
options: To guarantee that deleting an object through a base class pointer correctly invokes the derived class destructor
To make the class abstract and non-instantiable
To allow private variables to be inherited
questions.explanation: Without a virtual destructor, deleting a derived object via a base pointer causes undefined behavior and resource leaks.

questions.questionText: Which smart pointer in modern C++ (C++11+) maintains exclusive ownership of a dynamically allocated heap resource?
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr enforces exclusive ownership; it cannot be copied, only moved via std::move.

title: Relational Database Design & SQL Querying Assessment
description: Test complex SQL JOIN operations, GROUP BY aggregations, HAVING clauses, subqueries, and ACID properties.

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between WHERE and HAVING clauses in an SQL query?
options: WHERE is used for numeric comparisons, while HAVING is used for string comparisons
WHERE filters individual rows before aggregation; HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY
HAVING can only be used with SELECT * statements
WHERE requires an inner join to be present
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows prior to grouping; HAVING evaluates aggregate functions like COUNT() or SUM() after grouping.

questions.questionText: Which JOIN returns all records from the left table and matched records from the right table, filling with NULL when no match exists?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN (or LEFT OUTER JOIN) preserves all rows from the left table regardless of whether a matching record exists on the right.

title: HTML5 Semantic Markup & Modern CSS Layouts
description: Test HTML5 semantic structure, CSS Flexbox, CSS Grid, media queries, accessibility, and the CSS box model.

questions.questionText: When `box-sizing: border-box` is set on an element, what is included in the total declared width and height?
options: Content area only (padding and border are added externally)
Content, padding, and border (only margin is outside)
questions.explanation: border-box includes content, padding, and border within the specified element width and height.

questions.questionText: In CSS Flexbox, which property aligns items along the cross axis?
questions.explanation: align-items controls item alignment along the cross axis, while justify-content aligns along the main axis.

title: Data Structures & Algorithms Core Diagnostic
description: Evaluate Big-O time and space complexity, Linked Lists, Binary Search Trees, Stacks, Queues, and Graphs.

questions.questionText: What is the average-case time complexity of searching for an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explanation: In a balanced BST, each comparison halves the search space, giving an average search time complexity of O(log n).

questions.questionText: Which data structure operates on a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order?
questions.explanation: A Stack follows the LIFO principle where the most recently inserted item is the first one removed.
